one_liner: Discord provides voice, video, and text communication with APIs for building bots and integrations.

auth.notes: Discord supports OAuth2 with multiple grant types, bot tokens as bearer tokens, and basic auth (client_id:client_secret) for token endpoints.

evidence.snippet: Authenticating with the Discord API can be done in one of three ways: Using a bot token
We support the authorization code grant, the implicit grant, client credentials, and some modified special-for-Discord flows

access.notes: Developers can register applications and get credentials (client_id, client_secret, bot tokens) at no cost. Some advanced scopes and privileged intents require approval for verified apps (100+ guilds), but do not block initial development.

evidence.snippet: The first step in implementing OAuth2 is registering a developer application and retrieving your client ID and
Apps with fewer than 10,000 users can access privileged intents by enabling them in the Developer Portal.

api_surface.rate_limit_note: Per-route and global rate limits enforced with dynamic limits. Rate limit details provided via HTTP headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Reset, X-RateLimit-Bucket, X-RateLimit-Scope).

evidence.snippet: The Discord API is a REST API that allows you to interact with Discord data from your own applications.
Webhooks are a low-effort way to post messages to channels in Discord.
Rate limits exist across Discord's APIs to prevent spam, abuse, and service overload.

buildability.rationale: Self-serve free credentials, well-documented REST and WebSocket APIs, webhooks, and rate-limiting all support immediate toolkit development.

overview_evidence.snippet: Build bots and integrations on Discord, or connect your game with rich presence, voice chat, and more.
The Discord API is a REST API that allows you to interact with Discord data from your own applications.
